plan.contextChunk: This figure places two drawings of the same circuit side by side, labeled (a) and (b) beneath them. Each is a rectangle split by a single vertical wire into two adjacent loops. Two blue zigzag resistor symbols sit along the top wire, labeled R1 = 3.00 ohms on the left and R3 = 3.00 ohms on the right. The dividing branch carries R2 = 3.00 ohms and the right-hand vertical wire carries R4 = 4.00 ohms, while the left-hand vertical wire is a plain conductor. Two battery symbols sit along the bottom: V1 = 24.00 V in the left loop, plus terminal on the left, and V2 = 29.00 V in the right loop, plus terminal on the right. Panel (b) repeats every element unchanged and adds six teal dots at the corners and branch points, lettered a, b, and c across the top and f, e, and d across the bottom. Setting the bare circuit beside the lettered copy separates the physical layout from the labels laid over it. The pair prepares a multi-loop network for analysis with Kirchhoff's junction and loop rules, the two points where three wires meet serving as the junctions.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Kirchhoff analysis begins by marking nodes and paths on the same circuit; the equations come from conservation rules plus consistent sign choices, not from adding new components.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Use a wide textbook-style canvas with two matching circuits side by side, panel (a) on the left and panel (b) on the right, separated by generous horizontal space. Both panels should have the same rectangular two-loop geometry: a left loop and right loop share the central vertical branch. Keep wires black, resistor zigzags blue, batteries black with clear long/short plate symbols, and panel (b) node dots teal. Place component labels close to their components without overlapping wires: R1 above or just beside the upper-left resistor, R3 above the upper-right resistor, R2 beside the central vertical resistor, R4 beside the right vertical resistor, V1 below the lower-left battery, and V2 below the lower-right battery. Align battery polarities carefully: V1 has + on the left and − on the right; V2 has − on the left and + on the right. Node labels in panel (b) should sit just outside their teal dots: a upper-left, b upper center, c upper-right, f lower-left, e lower center, d lower-right. The interactive highlights, current arrows, loop paths, and equation boxes should augment panel (b) only while panel (a) remains visible as the unannotated reference. Use a warm orange or gold for loop tracing and junction branch highlights so they contrast with the teal node dots and blue resistor symbols.

authoredContext:
Consider the circuit in the figure(a). Let us analyze this circuit to find the current through each resistor. First, label the circuit as shown in part (b).

(a) A multi-loop circuit. (b) Label the circuit to help with orientation.

Part a shows a circuit with two horizontal branches and three vertical branches. The first horizontal branch has two resistors of 3 Ω each and the second branch has two voltage sources of 24 V with positive terminal on the left and 29 V with positive terminal on the right. The left vertical branch is directly connected, the middle branch has a resistance of 3 Ω and the right branch has a resistance of 4 Ω. Part b shows the same circuit as part a with labelled junctions

Next, determine the junctions. In this circuit, points b and e each have three wires connected, making them junctions. Start to apply Kirchhoff’s junction rule (∑ Iin=∑ Iout) by drawing arrows representing the currents and labeling each arrow, as shown in the figure(b). Junction b shows that I1=I2+I3 and Junction e shows that I2+I3=I1. Since Junction e gives the same information of Junction b, it can be disregarded. This circuit has three unknowns, so we need three linearly independent equations to analyze it.

demo_steps.title: Same circuit, two views

demo_steps.title: Trace the left loop

demo_steps.title: Trace the right loop

plan.keyInsight: Kirchhoff equations are not extra circuit components; they come from labeling the same nodes and consistently tracking current conservation at junctions and voltage signs around loops.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Draw one clean 2D circuit that can switch between the unlabeled and labeled versions rather than showing both full panels side by side. Use black straight wires, blue zigzag resistor symbols, and teal node dots with italic letter labels in the labeled view. Keep R1 on the upper-left branch, R3 on the upper-right branch, R2 on the central vertical branch, and R4 on the right vertical branch. Place V1 on the lower-left branch with + on the left and − on the right; place V2 on the lower-right branch with − on the left and + on the right. Junction highlights should emphasize only b or e and its three incident branches. Loop tracing should use a warm highlight color and a small equation box showing terms accumulating into a final loop equation, such as left loop: −I_ab R1 − I_be R2 + V1 = 0, and right loop: −I_bc R3 − I_cd R4 − V2 + I_be R2 = 0 for the chosen clockwise traversal and current arrows.
